(a) Concurrent first requests race to construct `DatasetRegistry`; the losers' registry is discarded after already having done S3 listing work, and any state cached on the discarded instance is silently orphaned — the exact hazard the neighbouring `voice_encoder_lock` was added to prevent. (b) Because `get()` takes the global lock before the cache lookup, a slow cold open of dataset B serializes every cache-hit request for dataset A behind it: one dataset's S3 latency becomes the whole service's. Neither the registry nor the `lancedb` connections are ever disposed, so the lifespan has nothing to clean up on shutdown.
findings.recommendation: Build the `DatasetRegistry` in the services' lifespan and put it on `AppState` at startup (it is already a per-app resource and the lifespan is the sanctioned place), removing the lazy branch from `dataset_handle` entirely. In `DatasetRegistry.get`, do the cache read outside the lock and use a per-dataset lock (or double-checked `setdefault` on a per-id `threading.Lock`) so a cold open of one dataset never blocks hits on another. Add a `close()` that disposes the cached `lancedb` connections and call it from the lifespan's post-`yield`.

findings.title: `configure_app_logging`'s logger allow-list has drifted from the fleet — `maintenance` opts in and gets nothing
findings.why: The module exists precisely because Python's root default of WARNING means an unraised logger never creates the LogRecord, so INFO never reaches the OTLP handler (obs.py:4-9). A service that calls the function and is missing from the list gets the failure the function was written to prevent, with no error and no warning — `maintenance`'s entire INFO lifecycle tier (`compaction_sweep`, orphan scan, reconcile) is silently dropped in production today. A hand-maintained list of package names with no test is guaranteed to drift again on the next service rename.
findings.recommendation: Stop hardcoding the list. Either raise the ROOT logger to INFO and rely on per-dependency suppression, or derive the set from an env var (`RASK_APP_LOGGERS`, defaulting to the caller's own top-level package via `__name__.partition('.')[0]`) so each service raises its own tree. At minimum, add `maintenance`/`ingest`/`flows`/`controlplane`/`compute`/`gateway`, delete `compaction` and `common`, and add a test that asserts every service package that calls `configure_app_logging` appears in the list.

findings.title: `make_service_app` reads `.env` and builds `Settings` at import time; settings are not injectable
findings.why: Configuration is bound at import, so a test cannot supply settings without mutating `os.environ` ahead of the import statement — the ordering hazard the conftest's `# noqa: F401` eager import exists to enforce, and the reason `test_slash_tolerance.py` has to re-derive its prefix from `build_settings()` rather than assert one. `load_dotenv()` at import also makes the effective configuration depend on the process working directory, which differs between `make test`, a container and CI. The lifespan seam the library already owns is the natural place for this.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional `settings: Settings | None = None` parameter to `make_service_app` (defaulting to `build_settings()`), so tests and alternative entrypoints can inject. Move `load_dotenv()` out of `build_settings` into the process entrypoint (or drop it — `pydantic-settings`' `env_file=".env"` in `Settings.model_config` already reads it). Consider having services expose `create_app()` rather than a module-level `app` singleton so import no longer has configuration side effects.

findings.title: Lifecycle invariants the shared probes depend on are unenforced convention, hand-rolled in every service
findings.why: The factory owns a wrapping lifespan and a shared probe router but delegates the contract between them to prose. A lifespan that forgets `startup_complete` makes `/readyz` return 503 forever — the pod never joins rotation — and the `getattr(..., False)` default guarantees that failure is silent rather than an AttributeError someone would notice in the first test run. A lifespan that forgets `app.state.settings` turns every `SettingsDep` route into a 500. Both are exactly the shared concerns the group's platform library is for, and both are currently copy-pasted 8+ times.
findings.recommendation: In `make_service_app`'s `wrapped` lifespan, set `app.state.settings = s`, `app.state.startup_complete = False`, `app.state.shutting_down = False` before entering the base lifespan; set `startup_complete = True` after it yields and `shutting_down = True` in the `finally`. Then delete the duplicated lines from the eight services and drop the `getattr` defaults in `probes.py` so a missing flag is a loud failure rather than a permanent 503. Services on the fastapi-template layout that build their own `FastAPI(...)` can call a small exported helper (`service_kit.lifecycle.lifecycle_flags(app)`) for the same guarantee.

findings.title: Name collision inside one package: two `Settings` classes and two `get_settings` with different DI shapes (`RASK_*` vs `MEDIA_*`)
Duplicate column-lineage builders + a same-named 3-tuple `ColumnEdge`, and stale TRANSITIONAL markers pointing at a gate whose target package now exists
`lancekit.store` builds a new `pyarrow.fs.S3FileSystem` per call and bypasses `packages/storage`
findings.why: Two problems. (a) A new S3 filesystem client per listing/stat call means credential resolution and connection setup repeated on every dataset open, and it is a second S3 access path parallel to `packages/storage`, which the house rules name as the canonical, provider-agnostic wrapper — a future endpoint/credential change now has two places to land, and this one hardcodes a `us-east-1` fallback. (b) An S3-backed root with unset `storage_options` reports "no datasets" and "does not exist" rather than erroring, which is the same silently-empty-listing failure `schemas/storage.py:93-98` explicitly criticises ("such a store fails with an auth error, which is at least a loud and explicable failure rather than a silently empty listing").
findings.recommendation: Construct the filesystem once per registry (pass it in, or memoize on the `DatasetRegistry`) instead of per call, and route it through `packages/storage` so endpoint/credential/region resolution has one owner and stays MinIO/HCP/AWS-agnostic. Replace the two silent-degradation branches with a raised `ValueError`/`RuntimeError` naming the missing `storage_options` — a URI root with no credentials is a misconfiguration, not an empty store.

findings.title: `Settings.storage_options` is a property that performs a blocking Dapr secret fetch and raises
findings.why: The name and the syntax promise a cheap attribute read; the implementation makes a network call to the Dapr sidecar and can raise `RuntimeError` — an exception type nothing in the handler chain maps, so it surfaces as a bare 500. Callers reasonably read it inside expressions and argument lists, where a raise is unexpected. The `@lru_cache` also pins the fetched secret for the process lifetime with no TTL, so a rotated credential is never picked up without a restart.
findings.recommendation: Make it an explicit method — `def resolve_storage_options(self) -> dict[str, str] | None` — so the I/O and the failure mode are visible at every call site, and raise `ServiceUnavailableError` (a `DomainError`) instead of `RuntimeError` so the fail-closed refusal renders as problem+json rather than a 500. Resolve it once in the lifespan and hand the resulting dict to the registry, rather than resolving per dataset open; if per-process caching stays, give `_store_secret` an explicit TTL or a documented restart-to-rotate contract.

findings.title: `RASK_*` env vars read directly via `os.environ` outside the settings modules
`_setup_logging` configures logger trees no package in the repo produces — `RASK_LOG_LEVEL` is inert
Lineage emitter logs under a hardcoded `"lineage"` logger and writes events straight to stdout
No `__all__` and no public/private marking: importing anything from `service_kit` executes the app factory module
Constrained settings validated by hand-rolled `field_validator`s instead of `StrEnum`/`Literal`
`dataset_handle` (the shared media resolution entry point, ~34 callers) has no return annotation — inside an explicitly ANN-exempt tree
Bare `except Exception` swallow-and-continue in three shared code paths
Stale references to deleted packages, migrated gates and a renamed frontend layout
CORS is registered first and therefore ends up the INNERMOST of five middleware layers
Idempotency of tuple writes/deletes is decided by substring-matching the OpenFGA error body, so a genuinely rejected write or revoke is swallowed AND audited as success
findings.why: `write_failed_due_to_invalid_input` appears in BOTH marker lists, so the same code is asked to mean two opposite things, and the bare substring `"does not exist"` also matches OpenFGA's undefined-relation/undefined-type validation text. That is exactly the hazard the module's own `grant_on_create` docstring warns about at :1134 (`parent` vs `tenant` — "a tuple OpenFGA accepts and no rule ever reads"): a delete carrying a mis-spelled relation is classified "already absent", skipped, and then emitted as an `access_tuple_delete` SUCCESS audit row. The live grant survives while the compliance trail says it was revoked — the stale-grant privilege bleed `revoke_object_tuples`'s own docstring (:1208) exists to prevent. On the write side a swallowed rejection leaves an object with no owner while `grant_on_create` returns success, which is the incident already recorded at :1038-1043.
findings.recommendation: Stop inferring idempotency from prose. openfga_sdk ships the supported primitive: pass `options={"conflict": ConflictOptions(on_duplicate_writes=ClientWriteRequestOnDuplicateWrites.IGNORE, on_missing_deletes=ClientWriteRequestOnMissingDeletes.IGNORE)}` to `client.write(...)` so the SERVER decides, and let every remaining 400 propagate as a real failure. If a client-side classifier must stay for older servers, key it on the structured `exc.code`/`error_message` field only (never `str(exc)`), require an exact code match, and add tests that a 400 with any other validation message is NOT swallowed. Either way, never `_audit_tuples` a tuple whose write/delete was not confirmed.

findings.title: Partial batch failure in write_tuples/delete_tuples skips the audit trail entirely for the tuples that DID land
findings.why: `_audit_tuples` is emitted once, AFTER the whole loop, so a failure on tuple 3 of 5 leaves tuples 1-2 written to (or removed from) OpenFGA with zero audit rows. That directly contradicts the guarantee the function's own docstring makes at :1015 — "a new write site cannot reach OpenFGA without passing through here" — and the gap opens precisely during an OpenFGA brown-out, when reconstructing what actually changed matters most. A repo-wide grep for `access_tuple_write` in tests returns no hits, so nothing detects the regression.
findings.recommendation: Audit per tuple at the moment it is confirmed, inside the loop, rather than once for the whole batch after it: move the `audit(...)` call to just after each successful `_do_write([item])` / `_delete_one(t)` (and after the single-shot transactional fast path). While there, stop auditing skipped already-absent deletes as `access_tuple_delete` successes — emit a distinct outcome or none. Add a test that a mid-loop failure still produces rows for the tuples that landed.

findings.title: expand_tree reports every repeated object#relation as `cycle: True`, so an ordinary concentric diamond is mislabelled a loop and its subtree is dropped
findings.why: `seen` is global to the walk, not per-path, so it deduplicates a DAG rather than detecting a cycle. In this model that fires on the normal case: `table.writer = ... or owner or writer from parent` and `namespace.writer = ... or owner or writer from parent`, so walking `table:x#reader` at depth>=3 reaches `namespace:db#owner` through both `table#owner -> owner from parent` and `namespace#writer -> computed owner`. The second arrival is stamped `cycle: True` and the branch loses the direct owner grants and the warehouse hop underneath it. `expand_tree` is the estate-admin "why does this person have access" primitive, so an operator reading one branch sees a dead end labelled as a misconfiguration where a real grant lives. `tests/unit/test_fga_expand.py:248` only builds a genuine a↔b loop, so nothing catches the diamond.
findings.recommendation: Track the visited set per PATH (pass a frozenset/tuple of ancestors down `_walk` and copy on descent) so only a true ancestor repeat is a cycle; if global dedup is wanted for cost, keep it but emit a distinct marker (`"seen_elsewhere": True` with the node name to cross-reference) so a shared subtree is not reported as a misconfiguration. Add a diamond test built from the real model shape. Separately, the fan-out at :787-790 awaits each `_walk` sequentially — once the visited set is per-path those legs are independent and can go through `asyncio.gather`.

findings.title: Two silent-truncation paths surface only to the log; the return value is indistinguishable from a complete answer
findings.why: Both docstrings claim the opposite of what the code delivers: `list_users` says "an under-reported review must never pass unnoticed" (:522) and `read_object_tuples` says "Surface it (a partial revoke must not look complete)" (:906). A log line is not a signal the CALLER can act on — the API consumer receives an ordinary list. An access review at the 1000-subject server cap silently under-reports who can reach an object, and a truncated `read_object_tuples` makes `revoke_object_tuples` return a count that reads as "all grants removed" while grants remain on a dropped-then-reused id — the exact stale-grant bleed that function exists to close.
findings.recommendation: Make partiality part of the type, not the log: return `(subjects, truncated: bool)` from `list_users` and `(tuples, complete: bool)` from `read_object_tuples`, and have `revoke_object_tuples` raise (or return a result object carrying `complete=False`) rather than a bare count when the read was truncated — a partial revoke must be a failure the caller sees. Add tests at both ceilings.

findings.title: governed/deps.py raises the FLEET exception taxonomy while its three sibling modules raise the Lance one — a latent off-contract 401/503 for any lance-plane service that adopts make_auth_deps (catalog/lineage/medallion/maintenance install only the Lance handlers; ingest and viewer install both)
findings.why: Two classes named `ServiceUnavailableError` are raised inside one auth flow. `install_problem_handlers` maps only `LanceNamespaceError`, and catalog / lineage / medallion / maintenance / ingest install it WITHOUT `service_kit.exceptions.register_handlers` (verified: only viewer, search and annotator install both). `make_auth_deps` is documented at deps.py:1-17 as the shared factory for "any governed service", so the first lance-plane service to adopt it gets a `{"detail": ...}` body with `application/json` and no `code` for exactly the 401/503 that a generated Lance Namespace client dispatches numerically — while the `fga.check` 503 raised two frames away renders as correct problem+json. `services/ingest/src/ingest/__init__.py:58-63` already records this class of bug in prose ("A DENIAL MUST BE A 403, NOT A 500").
findings.recommendation: Pick one taxonomy per plane and enforce it inside the package: have `governed/deps.py` raise `lance_namespace.UnauthenticatedError` / `ServiceUnavailableError` like its three sibling modules, so everything the governed layer emits is problem+json with a numeric code. If the fleet taxonomy must stay reachable, register a `DomainError` handler from `install_problem_handlers` itself (or add an `HTTPException` handler that re-shapes into problem+json) so no service can install one half of the contract. Add a test that builds a bare app with only `install_problem_handlers` and asserts the media type + `code` on a 401 and a 503 from the auth deps.

findings.title: The three-field retry triple and the fail-closed except block are copy-pasted through all thirteen FGA operations
findings.why: Thirteen signatures carry the identical three-field triple and eleven bodies carry the identical five-line fail-closed block; `expand_tree`, `revoke_object_tuples` and `grant_on_create` exist mostly to thread the triple down to the primitives they call (fga.py:732-738, 1219-1236, 1139-1147). The knowledge duplicated is one policy — "how this process retries OpenFGA and what it does when it gives up" — so every change to it is a thirteen-site edit, and the noise is a large part of why a 1237-line module reads as unnavigable. It also disperses the audit-gap and truncation bugs above across many near-identical bodies where one would do.
findings.recommendation: Bind the policy once instead of per call: a frozen Pydantic `RetryPolicy(attempts, backoff, max_backoff, overall_budget)` passed to `make_client` (or held beside the client in a tiny `FgaClient` wrapper), and one `_guarded(op_name, **log_fields)` async decorator/context manager that owns both the tenacity wrapper and the fail-closed translation. Each operation then shrinks to its SDK call, and the retry defaults stop appearing in thirteen signatures.

findings.title: make_client returns an aiohttp-backed OpenFgaClient with no disposal contract, and seven of its nine fleet call sites never close it (only lineage and the medallion mover do)
findings.why: `OpenFgaClient` owns an aiohttp `ClientSession`; leaving it unclosed leaks the connector and emits "Unclosed client session" at shutdown. Across the fleet `make_client` is called at nine lifespan sites (viewer, ingest ×2, medallion producer + mover, lineage, annotator, catalog, maintenance) and only ONE — `services/medallion/src/medallion/mover.py:73` — ever calls `await app.state.fga.close()`. When eight of nine consumers get the same thing wrong, the defect is the library's unstated contract, not eight independent oversights; the same package already models the correct shape in `UserStateStore.build`/`aclose`.
findings.recommendation: Give the factory a disposal contract the caller cannot miss: add an `@asynccontextmanager fga_client(...)` that yields the client and closes it, or at minimum a `close_client(client)` helper plus an explicit "the lifespan MUST await `client.close()` after yield" line in the `make_client` docstring. Then fix the eight leaking lifespans (out of this scope, but they are the reason this is filed here).

findings.title: Four hand-rolled object-store record registries with byte-identical hashed-key helpers and identical list-with-broad-except bodies
findings.why: Four modules independently implement the same primitive — one JSON document per record under a prefix, sha256-truncated key, put/get/delete/list, one-bad-record-skipped listing — and the estate already knows it: `warehouse_records.py:11` says "see the note in `protection.py` about collapsing these into one primitive". Duplicated knowledge means a fix to the record format, the key derivation, the tolerance policy or the S3 error handling has to be applied four times, and the four have already drifted (`protection` and `trash` use `stream.read()`, `maintenance_policies` and `warehouse_registry` use `stream.readall()`; only two carry the `# noqa: BLE001` rationale). The blanket `except Exception` also means a credential expiry mid-listing silently degrades to a shorter list for the maintenance sweep rather than an error.
findings.recommendation: Extract one `RecordStore` primitive in `lakehouse/` parameterised by prefix and a Pydantic record model — `put/get/delete/list_all` plus a single tolerant-listing policy that distinguishes a malformed record (skip, warn) from a store fault (propagate, so a sweep never mistakes an outage for an empty registry). Reimplement `protection`, `maintenance_policies`, `trash` and `warehouse_records` as thin typed facades over it; keep `warehouse_registry`'s resolution logic but let it read through the same store.

findings.title: Every lakehouse control-plane record is an unvalidated dict[str, Any]; write paths index required keys with no boundary validation
findings.why: Protection markers, maintenance policies, trash records and warehouse records are the estate's control plane — they decide what may be dropped, what gets compacted and reclaimed, and which bucket a tenant routes to — and none of them has a schema. The house rule is Pydantic for structured values; here the shape lives only in prose docstrings and in scattered `record.get(...)` calls, so `_record_is_well_formed` (maintenance_policies.py:115) exists precisely because nothing else validates, and `resolve_policy` (:170-192) must defensively re-check `isinstance(buckets, list)` on data it just read. A caller passing a wrong-shaped dict gets a `KeyError` deep inside the S3 write rather than a validation error at the boundary, and a field rename in the catalog's writer is invisible to every reader until a sweep quietly matches nothing.
findings.recommendation: Define one frozen Pydantic model per record kind (`ProtectionRecord`, `MaintenancePolicy`, `TrashRecord`, `WarehouseRecord`) in `lakehouse/`, validate on read (`model_validate_json`) and serialise on write (`model_dump_json`), and let the writers type their signatures against those models. Malformed rows then fail with a `ValidationError` that names the field, `_record_is_well_formed` collapses into the model, and the catalog↔maintenance contract becomes checkable by `ty` instead of by comment.

findings.title: Five direct os.environ reads outside any Settings class, three on the per-request path, plus an unprefixed env var and a hard-coded Dapr sidecar port
findings.why: The estate's rule is pydantic-settings + `@lru_cache get_settings` with a namespaced prefix, and this package already models it in `governed/settings.py`. Instead the security-critical `APP_API_TOKEN` and the public-front-door allowlist are read straight from the process environment on the request hot path — untestable through Settings, unvalidatable at boot, and rebuilding a `frozenset` per request. `WAREHOUSE_REGISTRY_TTL_SECONDS` carries no prefix at all, so it collides with anything else in the pod's environment and is invisible to an `env | grep RASK_`/`LANCE_` audit. The Dapr port defaults to a literal 3500 in two modules while daprd injects the authoritative `DAPR_HTTP_PORT` (which the `user_state` module docstring at :26 even names) — a non-default sidecar port silently breaks the secret and user-state paths.
findings.recommendation: Add the three knobs (`app_api_token`, `public_callers`, `warehouse_registry_ttl_seconds`) to the `GovernedAuthSettings` mixin (or a small sibling mixin) with `LANCE_*`/`RASK_*` aliases, and pass them into `require_dapr_token` / `service_principal` / `_resolve_root` as arguments the way the rest of this package does. Default `dapr_http_port` from `DAPR_HTTP_PORT` in the settings layer rather than a literal. Keep `assert_app_token_configured` as the boot-time fail-closed check, now reading the validated setting.

findings.title: Module-level mutable cache global in warehouse_registry with no bound and no eviction
findings.why: Entries are only ever inserted and overwritten — an expired entry is never evicted, so a project whose warehouse is deleted keeps its tuple resident for the life of the process, and the dict grows monotonically with the number of distinct `(control_root, project, serving)` triples the process has ever resolved. The house rule is `app.state` plus a dep wrapper rather than module globals holding mutable state; here the global also means two co-hosted apps in one process (the medallion producer hosts the train router) share and cannot separately invalidate a cache, and the only invalidation lever is a global `clear_cache()`.
findings.recommendation: Replace the bare dict with a bounded TTL cache owned by the caller: either a small `WarehouseResolver` object built in the lifespan and stashed on `app.state` (with its own `_cache` instance and an `invalidate(project)` method), or `cachetools.TTLCache(maxsize=..., ttl=...)` if the module-level shape must stay. Either way give it a maxsize and per-key invalidation so a deactivation can be pushed rather than only waited out.

findings.title: The JWKS fetch has no explicit timeout while the discovery fetch beside it does
findings.why: Every outbound call needs an explicit timeout. `PyJWKClient` falls back to its own 30 s default, and the fetch fires lazily inside `verify()` — i.e. on a live request whenever the JWK cache misses (cold start, key rotation, `max_cached_keys` eviction). Because `authenticate` is a sync FastAPI dependency it runs in Starlette's threadpool (default 40 workers), so a hung IdP can pin those workers for 30 s each and starve every sync route in the service, not just the authenticated ones. The module already got this right one line earlier for discovery, which makes the omission an inconsistency rather than a deliberate posture.
findings.recommendation: Pass `timeout=` to `PyJWKClient` (a value at or below the discovery client's, sourced from the same settings knob as `oidc_cache_ttl`/`oidc_leeway`), and consider a `lifespan_kwargs`-style single shared timeout constant so the two fetch paths cannot drift again. Add a test that a slow JWKS endpoint raises rather than hangs.

findings.title: lakehouse.sources.S3Source / sinks.S3Sink shadow the canonical storage.S3Source / storage.S3Sink by name with an incompatible API
findings.why: `packages/storage` is the estate's declared canonical S3 wrapper and exports `S3Source`/`S3Sink`/`FSSource`/`FSSink` at the top level; `service_kit.lakehouse` exports a second pair under the same two class names with a different constructor and a different method contract. Both are live — `services/ingest/adapters.py:109` and `services/medallion/services/media_produce.py:33` import service_kit's, while the ratch/HTR planes use storage's — so `from ... import S3Source` no longer identifies a type, and a reader (or an autocomplete) landing on the wrong one gets an object whose methods do not exist. The underlying seams genuinely differ (pyarrow-fs for the Lance plane, picklable boto3 for Ray actors), so this is a naming/ownership defect rather than redundant code.
findings.recommendation: Either rename the lakehouse pair to say what they are (`ArrowFsSource`/`ArrowFsSink`, or `PyArrowS3Source`/`PyArrowS3Sink`) so the two seams are distinguishable at the import line, or move them into `packages/storage` beside their siblings under those distinct names and have `service_kit.lakehouse` re-export the `SourceAdapter`/`SinkAdapter` Protocols only. Whichever way, one package should own the S3 adapter vocabulary.

findings.title: The entire audited scope sits under a blanket 21-rule ruff exemption declared temporary for verbatim-copied files that have since been rewritten in place
findings.why: Both subpackages in this scope are exempted from `ANN201`/`ANN202`/`ANN401` (the annotation gate the house rules lean on), `C901` (complexity — relevant to a 1237-line `fga.py` and to `resolve_policy`), `S110`/`S112` (try-except-pass / try-except-continue — relevant to the nine broad `except Exception` sites here) and `E501`. The justification recorded in pyproject is that these were "freshly-copied" lance-ns files not worth reformatting; but the code has since been substantially authored in place (the whole `expand`/`expand_tree`/`read_changes` surface, the outbox, the four registries), so the exemption now hides new debt rather than grandfathering old. Concretely it is why `_retrying` (fga.py:218) ships with no return annotation and why the swallow-and-continue sites are unflagged.
findings.recommendation: Narrow the exemption to what is still genuinely justified — `A002` (LanceDB public parameter names) and `ANN401` (untyped pyarrow/lance/dapr boundaries) — and drop `ANN201`/`ANN202`/`C901`/`S110`/`S112`/`E501` for `governed/**` and `lakehouse/**`, fixing the resulting handful of findings. Do it as one commit per subpackage so the diff stays reviewable, and update the docs/OPEN-WORK.md entry rather than leaving the note to outlive the reason.

findings.title: fetch_dapr_secret swallows every exception into an empty bundle and logs a boot-blocking failure at WARNING
Any/object on public signatures where a Protocol or Callable alias exists, and a decorator factory with no return annotation
S3Source re-implements its own listing-and-sort inline instead of calling the _listing helper it already has
`client.meta.events.unregister("needs-retry.s3")` is a proven no-op — the retry handler it means to remove is still registered
findings.why: The line carries no comment, so a reader cannot tell whether it was meant to disable boto's retries (which would conflict with the explicit `retries=` config on line 81 — a double-retry concern) or to strip the S3 region redirector (which matters against MinIO/RustFS, where a redirect on a missing bucket is nonsense). Either way the intended behaviour has never happened, and the estate has been shipping under the false belief that it did.
findings.recommendation: Decide the intent and express it truthfully: to drop a specific handler, pass it — `client.meta.events.unregister('needs-retry.s3', botocore.retryhandler.RetryHandler…)` or use `unique_id=`; to disable retries, set `retries={'max_attempts': 0}` in the `Config` and delete the line. Add a `s3_client` unit test that asserts the resulting handler set, so the next edit cannot silently no-op.

findings.title: storage's own error taxonomy is half-applied: `s3_errors` wraps nothing inside `packages/storage`, and `iiif.py` re-implements it inline
findings.why: The taxonomy exists precisely because a raw botocore exception escaping storage became an HTTP 500 with a traceback (the module docstring cites the 2026-07-28 live incident). Leaving the package's own primary read/write path unwrapped means the next consumer reproduces that incident, and the divergent inline code-set in `iiif.py` means a missing *bucket* is treated as a cache miss and silently backfilled from IIIF instead of being reported.
findings.recommendation: Wrap `S3Source.read`, `S3Sink.write`, `iter_keys` and `IIIFCachedSource.read`/`cached_keys` in `s3_errors(bucket=…, key=…)`, and replace the inline `getattr(exc, "response", …)` block in `iiif.py` with `except ObjectNotFoundError` / `except BucketNotFoundError` over the shared contextmanager so there is exactly one definition of each code set.

findings.title: Hand-rolled retry loop with `time.sleep` and a bare `assert` in `fetch_image`
findings.why: House rule 10 puts retries on one centralized mechanism (`tenacity`), not per-call `for i in range(attempts)` loops. This one has no jitter (synchronised thundering herd across the ~64 concurrent Ray readers the docstring describes), no total-duration cap, and terminates on an `assert` — which `python -O` strips, turning the exhausted-retries path into an `UnboundLocalError`-adjacent `raise None` (`TypeError: exceptions must derive from BaseException`) instead of the real transport error. The function-local `import time as _time` also hides the blocking sleep from a reader scanning imports.
findings.recommendation: Replace the loop with `@retry(retry=retry_if_exception_type(httpx.TransportError) | retry_if_result(...), stop=stop_after_attempt(3) | stop_after_delay(60), wait=wait_exponential_jitter(initial=1, max=10), before_sleep=before_sleep_log(log, WARNING), reraise=True)` from tenacity, keeping the existing 4xx-except-429 exclusion as the retry predicate. Delete the `assert`; tenacity's `reraise=True` gives the last exception with a real traceback.

findings.title: Three copies of the lazy-client/pickle dance and four copies of the `list_objects_v2` paginate loop, with no `Source`/`Sink` Protocol to anchor them
findings.why: Three implementations is exactly the Rule-of-Three trigger, and the missing Protocol is why the two public factory functions have to erase their return type — every downstream consumer of `build_source()` gets `Any`, so no type checker can catch calling `.write()` on a source. The paginate duplication is also where the bounded-listing bug class lives: `iter_keys` was made suffix-filterable and case-insensitive while `IIIFCachedSource.cached_keys` was not.
findings.recommendation: Define `class Source(Protocol): def keys(self) -> Iterable[str]: ...; def read(self, key: str) -> bytes: ...` and `class Sink(Protocol): ...` in a `storage/protocol.py`, annotate `build_source`/`build_sink` with them (dropping both `noqa: ANN401`), extract the lazy-client+pickle triple into a small `_LazyClient` mixin, and have `S3Source.keys`/`S3Sink.existing_keys`/`IIIFCachedSource.cached_keys` all delegate to the existing `iter_keys`.

findings.title: `derive_hcp_creds` mutates process-global `os.environ` to inject S3 credentials from env secrets
findings.why: A library function writing to `os.environ` is a process-wide, irreversible, non-thread-safe side effect: every other boto3/httpx/subprocess consumer in the process silently inherits credentials it never asked for, and a test that calls it (as `test_derive_hcp_creds` does) leaks them into the rest of the session. The name also lies about the side effect — `derive_` reads as pure. Separately, the secret source is plain env (`HCP_PASSWORD`), not the Dapr secret store the estate's ruling requires, and the failure mode is fail-open (unset → silent no-op → anonymous S3 that returns empty listings rather than erroring). The `md5` itself is dictated by the HCP backend and is not the defect.
findings.recommendation: Make it pure: `def hcp_creds() -> tuple[str, str] | None` returning the derived pair, and have `s3_client` pass them through the `access_key`/`secret_key` parameters it already accepts (client.py:56-57). Never write `os.environ` from a library. Track the secret-store migration separately under the fail-closed ruling.

findings.title: `packages/storage` declares `requires-python = ">=3.10"` but uses PEP 695 `type` syntax (3.12+) — the metadata is factually wrong
findings.why: A resolver honouring the declared floor will happily install `storage` on 3.10/3.11, where importing it fails at parse time. Inside the uv workspace this is masked because everything resolves to 3.13, so the lie is invisible until the package is consumed anywhere else (a sealed runner, an external tool, a published wheel) — which is precisely the scenario the `requires-python` field exists for.
findings.recommendation: Set `requires-python = ">=3.13"` on both `packages/storage` and `packages/validate` to match the workspace and the syntax actually in use.

findings.title: storage resolves env by hand (`os.getenv` tuples) instead of pydantic-settings — and lineage-kit's docstring cites storage as an example of the pattern it does not use
`python-dotenv` is a declared dependency of `packages/storage` and is never imported
`packages/tracker` has zero consumers and reintroduces the relational store P7a removed — while pulling sqlmodel + psycopg into the root lock
findings.why: House rule 7 (the P7a ruling) says no app relational DB in the fleet; this package is 359 lines of SQLAlchemy/SQLModel plus a real-Postgres test suite kept alive for no caller. It is already recorded as such at `OPEN-WORK.md:1284` ("packages/tracker has zero consumers and should probably die") and `open_ingest_design.md:414` rejects reviving it on four counts — so this is a confirmation, not a new discovery, but it is still live weight in the lock and in `testpaths`.
findings.recommendation: Delete the package, its workspace source entry, the `"tracker[postgres]"` root dependency, the `packages/tracker/tests` testpath, the `pytest-postgresql` dev dependency it alone needs, and the `tracker` entry in `known-first-party`. Git remembers it if the ingest plane ever wants the shape back.

findings.title: tracker's backend-agnostic contract is broken: the schema migration is SQLite-only, and DDL runs in the constructor with no migration path
findings.why: The stated contract (`models.py:20-22`: "shared across all SQLModel-compatible backends… the backend chooses the engine") does not hold: a Postgres database created before `etag`/`validated`/`verified` existed will silently keep the old table (`create_all` does not alter existing tables), and every `unverified_keys()`/`unvalidated_keys()` query then fails at the driver. `PRAGMA table_info` and `INTEGER DEFAULT 0` are SQLite dialect, so the fix cannot simply be lifted to the base class. Since Alembic was deleted at P7a there is no sanctioned migration path for the schema change either.
findings.recommendation: If the package survives PS-09, move the version check into a dialect-dispatched `_migrate()` on the base (inspecting via `sqlalchemy.inspect(engine).get_columns('transfer')`, which is backend-neutral) and make table creation an explicit `create_schema()` call rather than a constructor side effect. Otherwise this is subsumed by deleting the package.

findings.title: tracker owns an Engine + a long-lived Session but is not a context manager
`TrackerProtocol` omits `flush()`, which is in every backend's documented usage
`validate/rules.py` is entirely unconsumed — 5 exported symbols, 0 callers, 0 tests
findings.why: 86 lines of speculative "pluggable rules" plus a parallel Path-validator surface that no code path reaches, all of it exported from `__all__` so it reads as supported API. Its `validate()` function also shadows the package name, so `from validate import validate` is a live confusion trap.
findings.recommendation: Delete `rules.py` and its five `__all__` entries; keep the Path validators only if the ingest plane is about to use them, otherwise narrow the public surface to `ValidationError` + `validate_bytes_by_extension` + the three `*_bytes` functions the ingest path can reach.

findings.title: `@dataclass` used for a value object (Pydantic-only estate)
`ray_kit.submit` — deterministic ids and the reattach-or-resubmit branch — has no tests, despite its own docstring naming it the hard part
findings.why: Both failure modes are silent and expensive: if the duplicate-id branch never resubmits, a redelivered trigger re-observes the same FAILED job until JetStream's maxDeliver drops it and the work never runs; if it resubmits when it should reattach, one trigger becomes N jobs on the cluster whose history already OOMKilled the compute service once. `submit_or_reattach` has four distinct paths (2xx, duplicate+terminal-bad, duplicate+live, non-duplicate 4xx) and none is exercised.
findings.recommendation: Add `packages/ray-kit/tests/test_submit.py` driving `submit_or_reattach` over an `httpx.MockTransport`: assert (a) a 2xx posts once, (b) a 4xx with an existing FAILED job issues DELETE then a second POST, (c) a 4xx with a RUNNING job reattaches and posts nothing more, (d) a 4xx with no existing job raises `RayJobError`. Pin `submission_id` determinism and its `[^A-Za-z0-9_-]` sanitisation + 200-char truncation.

findings.title: Independent dashboard GETs are awaited sequentially in three functions
findings.why: Latency is doubled on every poll of three endpoints the compute zone polls on a timer (`list_tasks`'s sibling comment notes a 5 s poll from two pages). The `/api/v0/actors?limit=1000` and `/logical/actors` responses are both large; serialising them is pure wall-clock waste against a dashboard that is already the estate's slowest dependency.
findings.recommendation: Use `asyncio.gather(..., return_exceptions=True)` (or a `TaskGroup` with per-branch handling) for each pair, keeping the existing best-effort semantics: the primary call's failure still returns `ok=False`, the secondary's still degrades to omitted telemetry.

findings.title: `logs()` reports `ok=True, "(empty or unavailable)"` for every status ≥ 400 — a 401 from a token-authed dashboard renders as an empty log file
findings.why: The comment justifies the branch for ONE upstream quirk (500 on empty files) but the predicate swallows the entire 4xx/5xx range. `auth.py`'s module docstring states the dashboard answers "401 when missing, 403 when invalid" under `RAY_AUTH_MODE=token` — so a misconfigured or rotated token makes every node log read as a successfully-fetched empty file, with `ok=True`. That is the least debuggable failure available: the operator sees "no logs" and looks at Ray, not at auth.
findings.recommendation: Narrow to the known quirk — treat only `500` (or better, a 500 whose body matches Ray's empty-file signature) as the empty note, and return `ok=False` with the status code for 401/403/404 and other 5xx, matching the sibling functions' `error=` shape.

findings.title: `job_logs` catches bare `Exception` while its six siblings catch `RAY_TRANSIENT_ERRORS`
findings.why: The wider catch turns any programming error inside the call — an `AttributeError` on an SDK version bump, a `TypeError` from a changed signature — into a benign `ok=False, error="…"` 200 response, so a real regression looks identical to "Ray is briefly unreachable" and never surfaces as a 5xx or a trace error. It also contradicts the tuple's own docstring, which exists to centralise this decision.
findings.recommendation: Use `except RAY_TRANSIENT_ERRORS as exc:` and delete the now-redundant comment; if the SDK genuinely raises something outside the tuple for unknown ids, add that class to `RAY_TRANSIENT_ERRORS` where the decision is documented.

findings.title: `cluster_status` is a 78-line function with a nested try inside a try inside a loop, doing five things
findings.why: Design-patterns puts the split threshold at 20-50 lines / 3+ nesting levels / multiple purposes; this hits all three. It is also the group's least-tested code — the whole function, `_parse_logical`, `_parse_res_value` and `_assign_physical_gpus` have no unit tests — and it already carries two comments describing bugs that were found in production (`clusterStatus: null` crashing `.get`, and the placement-group suffix silently dropping GPU counts), which is what a function this shape produces.
findings.recommendation: Extract `_fetch_cluster_usage(http, url) -> tuple[dict, dict]`, `_fetch_nodes(http, url) -> list[RayNode]` and `_fill_totals_from_nodes(total, used, nodes) -> None`, leaving `cluster_status` as a ~15-line composition; unit-test the three parsers directly against captured Ray JSON (they are pure).

findings.title: The error-payload string is copy-pasted eight times across `dashboard.py`
`proxy()` returns the raw, untruncated exception string — including the internal dashboard URL — to the browser
Orphaned `#:` doc-comment in `submit.py` documents a constant that no longer exists
Dropped lineage events have no signal but a log line — and the authoring step sits inside the transport try/except
findings.why: "Emission never crashes compute" is the right contract, but the current implementation makes total provenance loss indistinguishable from healthy operation at the fleet level — the only artefact is a WARNING on a Ray worker's stdout, in a governed deployment whose whole premise is that lineage is complete. The estate has already been bitten by exactly this failure twice. Secondarily, `event.to_openlineage()` is *inside* the try, so a model/serialisation defect (a facet the official client rejects) is reported as `lineage_emit_failed` — i.e. a code bug is disguised as a transport hiccup and every event for that shape is dropped for the process's lifetime.
findings.recommendation: Move `event.to_openlineage()` above the `try` so authoring errors propagate as the bugs they are. Add an OTel counter (`meter.create_counter("rask.lineage.emit.failures")` with bounded attributes: `state`, `transport`) incremented in the handler, so a dashboard can alert on drop rate; the package already depends on nothing OTel-shaped, so gate it behind a soft import or expose a `on_drop` callback the fleet's `setup_otel` path wires.

findings.title: The parent-resolution + namespace-defaulting ladder is copy-pasted in three modules
findings.why: Three copies is the Rule-of-Three trigger, and this particular knowledge — how a run picks its namespace and composes its dotted job name — is the linkage contract the whole package exists to guarantee. A change applied to two of three sites would produce runs that link correctly in the offline shape and detach in the online one, which is exactly the class of bug the linkage tests are long enough to miss. The repeated function-local import (three sites, each with the same apologetic comment) is a circular-import workaround made permanent.
findings.recommendation: Extract one helper — `def open_child_run(name, *, parent, namespace, emitter, run_facets=None) -> LineageRun` in `runs.py` — and have `stage.open_run`, `LineageActorMixin.init_lineage` and `job_run` all call it. Import `LineageSettings` at module top in that single home (there is no cycle: `config` imports nothing from `runs`).

findings.title: `LineageSettings()` is re-instantiated on every run-open in three lineage-kit paths — no cached accessor
`consume.py` imports the private `_Model` across a module boundary
None of the five packages ships a `py.typed` marker
The whole package has zero tests and is not even wired into pytest's testpaths
findings.why: 7,582 lines across 55 files, including the one sanctioned package CLI and all the Lance write paths (`core/dataset.py` is described as the single seam that makes create-time invariants unforgettable), carry no executable guarantee at all. Because the path is missing from `testpaths` AND pytest runs with explicit paths (`--import-mode=importlib`, no discovery), a test added under `packages/ratch/tests/` would silently never run — the gate is not merely empty, it is disconnected. The `Protocol` seams (`EmbeddingClient`, `CaptionClient`, `SummarizeClient`) and the zero-arg `factory` parameters threaded through `core/driver.py` exist specifically to permit offline fakes, so the design cost was already paid; only the tests are absent. The four docstrings asserting coverage actively mislead a reader into trusting behaviour nothing verifies.
findings.recommendation: Add `packages/ratch/tests` to `testpaths` in the root `pyproject.toml` in the same commit as the first test, so the wiring can never drift from the intent again. Start with the pure functions that need no Lance fixture (`retrieval/search.py`'s `extract_query_terms`/`timecode`/`parse_alignments_json`, `modalities/av/frames._jpeg_dimensions`, `features/topic_tree._nest`/`_subtree`, `lineage.column_map`), then the injectable seams the docstrings already promise: drive `features/embed_columns.embed_text_column` with a fake `EmbeddingClient` over a tmp_path Lance table, and `core/driver`'s resume paths (`_ValueCheckpoint` round-trip, the `take_blobs`-short-payload guard at `driver.py:109`) with a synthetic dataset. Delete or correct the four docstrings that name tests which do not exist.

findings.title: `ratch feature topics` reads the columns a fire-and-forget Ray Job has not written yet
findings.why: With `RATCH_RAY_ENABLED=1` (the documented cluster mode — `jobs.py:19-24` and `runners.py:14-16` both name it), `run_runner` returns milliseconds after `submit_job`, so `build_topic_tree` scans `chunks.lance` before the Toponymy worker has committed anything. On a first run this raises `ValueError("no topic_l* columns … run 'ratch feature topics' first")` from inside the very command that IS `feature topics` — a self-contradicting error. On a re-run over a corpus that already has `topic_l*` columns it is worse than a crash: it silently rebuilds the tree from the PREVIOUS run's stale labels and reports success, because `overwrite_dataset(topics_path, table)` (topic_tree.py:117) unconditionally overwrites. The in-process branch (`ray_enabled=False`, `jobs.py:126-128` → `_run_in_process`) blocks correctly, so the bug only appears in the mode the docstrings call the intended one — exactly where nothing tests it.
findings.recommendation: The submit-and-ack ruling is fine for a mover whose downstream is woken by the commit event, but `_run_topics` is a synchronous CLI step that consumes the output directly. Either (a) split the command so the tree build is a separate invocation that the job's completion event triggers (the shape `topic_tree` already exists for — `FEATURES["topic_tree"]`, columns.py:397), and have `_run_topics` return after dispatch with a message saying so; or (b) give `run_runner` an explicit `wait: bool` (defaulting to the current behaviour) and have `_run_topics` pass `wait=True`, restoring the terminal-status poll that `_TERMINAL_STATUSES`, `ray_job_timeout_seconds` and `ray_poll_interval_seconds` are still declared for. Do not leave the read immediately after the dispatch.

findings.title: Every `AWS_*` env var — including the secret access key — is copied into the Ray Job's runtime_env
findings.why: `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` and `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` match that prefix and land verbatim in the job's `runtime_env.env_vars`. Ray persists the submitted runtime_env in the job record and serves it back through the dashboard's job API (`GET /api/jobs/<submission_id>`) and the Jobs UI — and `JobsSettings.ray_address` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:8265` (:70), the unauthenticated Ray dashboard this repo runs (CLAUDE.md: "No auth, no app middleware. The services assume localhost / trusted network"). So a long-lived credential is written into a queryable, plaintext, persisted control-plane record every time a runner is dispatched. This is precisely the env-var secret propagation HOUSE-RULE-7 forbids: the Dapr/OpenBao secret store is the sole sanctioned source, fail-closed, and the memory note is explicit — "OpenBao via Dapr is the SOLE source, fail-closed; no env fallback".
findings.recommendation: Stop forwarding a credential-bearing prefix wholesale. Narrow `_FORWARDED_ENV_PREFIXES` to non-secret configuration only (`MEDIA_`, plus explicitly named non-secret S3 knobs like `RASK_S3_ENDPOINT_URL`/`AWS_REGION`/`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION` via an allow-list of exact names, not a prefix), and have the runner obtain its store credentials the same way the fleet does — from the Dapr secret store at worker start, failing closed if absent. If the local dev loop genuinely needs creds on the worker, that belongs in the cluster's own secret material (a k8s Secret mounted into the Ray worker pod), never in a per-job submission body.

findings.title: The library reaches into `runners/*` and three `services/*` modules that are not — and by ruling cannot be — its dependencies
findings.why: The root `pyproject.toml:26-29` states the ruling plainly: "NOTE: runners/* are deliberately NOT members — sealed model envs whose heavy pins (CUDA torch, model SDKs) must never enter the services' resolution", and `runners/asr/pyproject.toml` pins `torch==2.11.0+cu128` behind a private index with `requires-python = ">=3.10,<3.13"` — incompatible with ratch's `>=3.13`. So `ratch transcribe` and `ratch detect-language` can never import successfully from a correctly-provisioned ratch env; they raise a bare `ModuleNotFoundError` traceback rather than the actionable `RunnerJobError` that `core/jobs.py:213-218` was written to give ("runner {job.runner!r} is not importable here … Run it in its sealed env"). The dependency is also circular: `runners/diarize/diarize.py:32` does `from ratch.modalities.av.wav import extract_wav_16k_mono` while `cli/speaker.py:85` imports back the other way. `runners_root()`'s `parents[5]` compounds it — verified to resolve to `/home/blackwell/Desktop/rask` in the checkout, but to `/venv` for a `site-packages/ratch/core/runners.py`, so the whole runner seam is silently checkout-only. `cmd_serve` is the same defect one layer worse: it `Popen`s `viewer`/`search`/`annotator` (which do exist at `services/<n>/src/<n>/main.py` with a `run`) from ratch's interpreter, though none is a ratch dependency.
findings.recommendation: Route every runner through the seam that already exists and already produces a good error: `core.jobs.run_runner(RunnerJob(runner="asr", …))`, exactly as `_run_topics` does for `topics` — deleting the direct `from runners.… import` lines in `cli/transcribe.py` and `cli/speaker.py`. That also removes the circular edge, since `runners.*` may keep importing `ratch`. Replace `runners_root()`'s `parents[5]` with an explicit, overridable setting on `RunnersSettings` (e.g. `runners_root: Path` from `RATCH_RUNNERS_ROOT`, defaulting to the walk) so an installed wheel fails loudly instead of pointing at `/venv`. Drop `cmd_serve` entirely — three services are started by `scripts/dev-micro.sh`, which CLAUDE.md names as the source of truth for the fleet's process list, and a `packages/` library has no business supervising service processes.

findings.title: Every vLLM client opens an httpx connection pool that nothing ever closes
findings.why: There are eight construction sites and zero release sites. In `features/columns._run_embedding_feature` (:134) the client is a local that goes out of scope while `add_columns` is still streaming; the pool survives on the GC's schedule for the rest of a run that the module docstrings describe as taking hours. Inside a Ray actor the leak is structural rather than incidental — `ray_bindings.text_embed_compute` (:31) closes over `client` in the returned `compute`, so the actor holds the pool for its whole lifetime with no teardown hook, and `driver._map_batches` recreates actors between stages. This is exactly the resource-management rule the skills state without qualification: "Always use context managers for resources needing cleanup" and "Clean up unconditionally". The care taken elsewhere in this package (`_ValueCheckpoint.cleanup()`, `blob as handle` in `driver.py:102`, `with tmp.open("wb")` in `download.py:63`) makes the omission look accidental, not deliberate.
findings.recommendation: Give `VLLMTransport` `__enter__`/`__exit__` delegating to `httpx.Client`'s own context manager, and forward the same on the four clients (they already have `close`, so it is three lines each). Then use them: `with VLLMEmbeddingClient(...) as client:` in the three `features/columns._run_*` dispatchers. For the Ray actors, close over the transport and release it in the actor's teardown, or accept the actor-lifetime pool explicitly with a comment — but pick one and say so, rather than leaving a `close()` that no code path reaches.

findings.title: No retry or backoff anywhere on the model-server HTTP boundary, in a pipeline designed for hours-long runs
findings.why: Timeouts are set correctly everywhere (`DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S = 120.0`, `httpx.Timeout(timeout, connect=30.0)`) so the first half of the rule holds; the retry half is simply absent. A single 503 from a vLLM server restarting mid-batch — or one `ReadTimeout` while the GPU is saturated by another tenant — kills the Ray task, and `driver.run_blob_column_stage` has no per-batch error containment, so the whole stage aborts. `_ValueCheckpoint` bounds the *data* loss to the in-flight batch (`engine.py:41-49` was written for exactly this), which means the missing retry costs an operator-visible restart rather than corruption — but it makes an entirely routine transient into a manual intervention on a job the code itself says "can take hours: each value is one Gemma call". `download.py` is worse-behaved still: its `except Exception` at :69 converts a transient `ReadTimeout` into a permanent `"error: ReadTimeout"` bucket entry with no second attempt on a multi-gigabyte transfer.
findings.recommendation: Add `tenacity` and put ONE decorator at the single chokepoint that already exists — `VLLMTransport.post` — with `retry_if_exception_type((httpx.ConnectError, httpx.ReadTimeout, httpx.RemoteProtocolError))` plus a `retry_if_result` on `{429, 500, 502, 503, 504}`, `wait_exponential_jitter(initial=1, max=30)`, `stop_after_attempt(4)`, and `before_sleep=before_sleep_log(logger, WARNING)` so retries are never silent. Do not add a second layer in the clients or the drivers — one layer only. Give `download._download_one` the same treatment for its network exceptions, keeping `http 404` permanent.

findings.title: Three env-var namespaces, ten import-time `os.getenv` reads (plus two in-function), and no cached settings accessor
findings.why: `MEDIA_*`, `RATCH_*` and `AWS_*` coexist in one package while CLAUDE.md states "Env vars are `RASK_*`" and "Identifiers and env vars carry no `ra-`/`ra_` prefix" — an operator has no single `env | grep` that shows this package's configuration. The import-time binding is the sharper problem: `pydantic-settings` reads env at instantiation, but a module-level `os.getenv` reads it at import, so setting `MEDIA_EMBED_URL` after `import ratch` (a test, a notebook, a Ray worker that inherits env after module load) is silently ignored — the configuration.md gotcha, one level worse. The `cli/pipeline.py:21-24` duplication means the same four variables are read twice with two different names, and a future change to one default won't reach the other. `RunnersSettings()` is also re-parsed on every `runner_ray_remote_args` call rather than cached.
findings.recommendation: Collapse all of it into one `ratch/config.py` holding a single `RatchSettings(BaseSettings)` with `env_prefix="RASK_RATCH_"` (or `RASK_` with explicit field aliases) carrying `embed_url`/`summarize_url`/`caption_url`/`rerank_url`/`caption_model`/`caption_instruction` alongside the existing `ray_enabled`/`ray_address`/`runner_isolation`, exposed through a module-level `@lru_cache def get_settings() -> RatchSettings`. Have the clients take the URL as an already-required constructor argument (they already do — `embed_url: str = DEFAULT_EMBED_URL`) and let the `_run_*` dispatchers and `cli/pipeline.py` be the only readers of `get_settings()`, deleting the four duplicated `_DEFAULT_*` constants. Keep the `127.0.0.1:800x` values as Settings field defaults, which is sanctioned; just stop reading them at import.

findings.title: Two whole modules and four helpers/settings with no caller anywhere in the repo
findings.why: The house style is explicit — "If it's not called, delete it. No 'just in case' code. Git remembers everything" — and the cost here is not bytes but false signal. `lineage.py` looks like a wired lineage path to anyone auditing the estate's lineage coverage; it emits nothing. The three orphaned `jobs.py` items are worse: they make the module read as though it still polls to completion, which is exactly the misreading that hides finding ratch-002 — a reviewer sees `_TERMINAL_STATUSES`, a timeout setting, a poll interval and a failure-message extractor and reasonably concludes the job is awaited. `read_descriptor` being dead means the `lance_media.descriptor` stamp that `dataset.py`'s docstring calls one of three create-time invariants is written but never read back by this package.
findings.recommendation: Delete `_failure_message`, `ray_job_timeout_seconds`, `ray_poll_interval_seconds` and correct the `RunnerJobError` docstring — or restore the poll (see ratch-002) and use all four. Delete `ingest/sources.py` outright (see ratch-009 — the maintained copy is `service_kit.lakehouse.sources`). For `lineage.py`, either wire the one call its own docstring specifies ("The one call the driver would add after a successful stage write", :148-149) into `core/driver.py`'s three drivers, or move it out of the shipped package until it is wired — a DRAFT that imports cleanly and does nothing is indistinguishable from a feature.

findings.title: `ratch/ingest/sources.py` is an untested fork of the maintained `service_kit.lakehouse.sources`
findings.why: The forks have already diverged: service-kit has grown `KeyedSourceAdapter` (:34) for cheap enumeration without fetching, which `services/ingest`'s `iter_unit_keys` depends on; ratch's copy does not have it and never will, because nothing exercises it. Conversely ratch's copy carries `sniff_mime` + `_SIGNATURES` (:83-118) that service-kit lacks, so neither file is a superset — a future reader cannot tell which is authoritative. This is duplicated *knowledge* (what a source adapter is, how MIME is decided for the agnostic-blob contract), which is the case the DRY rule says to unify, not the coincidental-shape case it says to leave alone. It also violates the workspace memory note directly: "packages/storage is the canonical S3 wrapper" and shared abstractions belong in one place.
findings.recommendation: Delete `packages/ratch/src/ratch/ingest/sources.py`. If `sniff_mime` is worth keeping — it is the only part with no service-kit equivalent — move it (with `_SIGNATURES`) into `service_kit.lakehouse.sources` next to the adapters it belongs with, where `services/ingest` and `services/medallion` can reach it and where the existing suites will cover it. Nothing in ratch imports the module today, so the deletion needs no call-site migration.

findings.title: Index-build failures are swallowed at DEBUG and one helper is a literal `except Exception: pass`
findings.why: `logger.debug` is below the CLI's own configured level — `cli/_app.py:48-52` calls `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, …)` — so these messages are unconditionally invisible to every user of the tool. The consequence is not cosmetic: the comments at `ingest.py:425-429` and `cli/media.py:174-177` explain that these BTREE indexes back `doc_id`/`audio_path` lookups and that without them "filters silently fall back to full scans", and `cli/speaker.py:161-165` says the same for the diarization endpoint. So a broken index build produces exactly the symptom the code exists to prevent, with no trace. `except Exception` also catches `MemoryError` and any genuine bug in the Lance call, not just the "already exists / unsupported column" cases the authors had in mind. `frames.py:89`'s `pass` is the canonical anti-pattern verbatim; its `return 0, 0` fallback is defensible (dimensions are metadata only, as the docstring says) but the silence is not.
findings.recommendation: Raise the level to `logger.warning` at all four index sites so a skipped index is visible at the CLI's configured level, and name the specific exception Lance raises for the tolerated case rather than `Exception` (catch that, let everything else propagate). In `_jpeg_dimensions`, narrow to the parse errors actually possible — `struct.error` and `IndexError` — and drop the `pass` so the `return 0, 0` reads as the deliberate fallback the docstring promises. `projection.py:183`'s `except Exception` around the EVōC label-prop init is the one acceptable member of this set (it logs at WARNING and has a documented random-init fallback); leave it, but narrow it if EVōC's failure mode is known.

findings.title: `Stage.client` declares the capability the composition root should bind, and the composition root ignores it
findings.why: The registry docstring states the contract — "The core owns WHAT a stage consumes and produces (tables, columns, MIME gate, **client capability**, actor sizing); the composition root … owns HOW, by injecting the concrete compute factory" (registry.py:4-8) — and the composition root does not honour it. The declared indirection therefore buys nothing while costing the thing it was meant to prevent: adding a ninth stage requires editing `bind_column_stage`'s `match` even when it reuses an existing capability, because the binding is keyed to a unique name rather than to `"embed"`. Note the duplication this already causes — `text_embedding` and `caption_embedding` are both `client="embed"` yet need two near-identical `case` arms and two near-identical factories (`text_embed_compute` at :28 and `caption_embed_compute` at :39 differ only in which column they read). `Stage.client` is currently a decorative field whose only effect is a column in a help table, and a reviewer reading the registry will believe a dispatch exists that does not.
findings.recommendation: Make `bind_column_stage` dispatch on the declared capability, keyed by `(stage.client, the read column)` rather than the stage name: a module-level `dict[str, Callable]` from capability → factory-builder, with the column to read taken from `stage.read_columns[0]` — which collapses `text_embed_compute` and `caption_embed_compute` into one parameterised factory and makes `Stage.client` load-bearing. Do the same for `ray_av.run_append_stage`'s `extract_frames` branch (`client="frames"`). If instead the name-keyed dispatch is genuinely wanted, delete `Stage.client` from the model and from all eight stage declarations, and drop the column from `pipeline plan` — do not keep a field the docstring calls a contract and the code never reads.

findings.title: Six functions run 65-120 lines doing several distinct jobs, two of them near-duplicates of each other
findings.why: The stated bar is 20-50 lines and one purpose, with "deeply nested logic (3+ levels)" as an extract trigger. The concrete cost is visible in the speaker pair: because the resume/limit/resolve logic was copied rather than shared, the two commands have already drifted — `cmd_extract_speaker_turns` logs a `--jobs` warning and builds its BTREE inline with a swallowed exception (:170-173), while `cmd_embed_speaker_turns` delegates to `speaker_embeddings_indexes` (:349); one validates `--batch-size` (:254) and the other validates nothing. A fix to the resume semantics must now be made twice, and nothing tests either. `cmd_serve` (search.py:70-114) additionally hides four function-level imports (`os`, `subprocess`, `sys` at :82-84, then `time` at :92 mid-body) and a busy-wait supervisor inside a command whose declared job is "launch the services".
findings.recommendation: Extract the three shared speaker helpers into `cli/speaker.py` module scope — `_reset_or_resume(db, table_name, path, only_null) -> tuple[bool, set[str]]`, `_apply_limit(docs, limit)`, `_resolve_sources(pairs, audio_root) -> list[tuple[str, Path]]` — and have both commands call them; that alone takes ~60 lines out of the pair and removes the drift. In `run_scan_column_stage`, lift the blob-table precondition block (:219-234) into a `_prepare_blob_column(ds, stage, name) -> lance.LanceDataset | None` guard so the happy path is flat. In `ingest_many`, split the index building (`_build_chunk_indexes(table, fts_language)`) and the documents write, leaving the function as the four-line orchestration its docstring describes. Move `cmd_serve`'s imports to module scope or delete the command per ratch-004.

findings.title: Two ffmpeg subprocesses run with no timeout while every sibling ffmpeg call sets one
findings.why: `generate_thumbnails` (:93) walks `input_dir.rglob("*")` over a whole media corpus and calls one of these two per file. `ffmpeg` seeking into a truncated or malformed MP4 — precisely the case a bulk `ratch download` produces when a transfer is interrupted, and `download.py:70-71` only unlinks `.part` files, not partial `.mp4`s that were renamed — can block indefinitely on read. With no timeout the whole `ratch thumbnail` run hangs on one bad file with no output and no way to know which, since the per-file `logger.info` at :114 is written only *after* the call returns. The inconsistency is the tell: the author knew to bound `extract_chunk_frame` and `extract_wav_16k_mono` and missed the two here.
findings.recommendation: Give both helpers a `timeout: float = 60.0` parameter and pass it to `subprocess.run`, catching `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` and returning `False` so the file lands in the existing `"failed"` bucket that `generate_thumbnails:112` already reports — the function's contract (`{status: [stem, ...]}` with a `"failed"` key) already accommodates it, so no caller changes. While there, note `_extract_video_frame` and `_render_waveform` differ only in the ffmpeg filter arguments and the destination; folding them into one `_run_ffmpeg_thumbnail(cmd_tail, src, dest)` removes the second copy of the timeout fix.

findings.title: The library's FTS default is English while the CLI, the reindex path and the engine all default Swedish
findings.why: `ingest_many` and `ingest_document` are the package's public API — both are re-exported from `ratch/__init__.py:3` and `__all__` (:35-36) — so any programmatic caller that does not pass `fts_language` builds the corpus FTS index with the stemmer the code itself documents as wrong for this data. The failure is silent and only observable as reduced recall: as the same help text explains, Swedish inflections like `ministern` never reduce to a shared stem, so those queries "return zero hits". The CLI happens to shield the common path by passing `"Swedish"` explicitly, which is exactly why the divergence has survived — the one caller that would expose it overrides the default. `features/indexing.py` calls its Swedish value "the corpus FTS contract", making the ingest default a contract violation by the module's own vocabulary.
findings.recommendation: Change the two `"English"` defaults to `"Swedish"` so all six sites agree, or better: import `FTS_LANGUAGE` from `features/indexing.py` — already labelled the corpus contract — and use it as the default in `ingest_many`, `ingest_document`, `reindex_fts` and `ensure_fts_index`, so the value lives once. If the language should be corpus-configurable rather than pinned, it belongs on the settings object from ratch-007, not as four independently-typed literal defaults.

findings.title: The Typer CLI prints through 54 bare `typer.echo` calls and hand-rolls column widths; `rich` is not a dependency
`_run_in_process` passes arguments by mutating the global `sys.argv`
Three modules import a leading-underscore private symbol across a module boundary
Legacy `TypeVar` generics in the shared HTTP transport instead of PEP 695
`_gate_filter` inlines every admitted doc id into one unbounded SQL `IN` list

cross_service.title: DECISION ITEM: the estate runs three entrypoint families, two error taxonomies, three health conventions and two OTel wiring paths — the split is wider than the two sanctioned layouts
cross_service.why: Coexistence of the two sanctioned layouts is a ruling, not a defect — but the *number* of axes that vary is what makes a reviewer unable to predict any service's shape from knowing its family, and it is the root cause of findings X4, X5, X8, X9 and X11 below (each is a per-family convention that one member silently missed). A single documented table of 'family → entrypoint module, layout, handlers, probe paths, otel path' would turn each of those into a lint or a test rather than an audit discovery.
cross_service.recommendation: Do not unify the two layouts (that is a ruling). DO pin the axes that are accidental rather than chosen: (a) one entry module name per family — rename `maintenance/service.py` → `main.py` and give medallion a `main.py` that selects producer/mover, or record why not; (b) decide whether medallion/maintenance adopt `api/v1/endpoints/` or whether catalog-family services may stay flat, and write it in `.claude/skills/rask-architecture`; (c) add a `tests/unit` gate asserting, per service, which handler installer and which probe paths its app object exposes, so a new service cannot pick a fourth combination.

cross_service.title: `services/catalog/tests` and `services/lineage/tests` are not in `testpaths` — 18 tests guarding a commit-replay duplication bug and a privilege-escalation bug have never run
cross_service.why: `make test` / `make test-slow` pass no path arguments, so pytest uses `testpaths` — these three files are inert. Two of them pin security properties (a shared app-token could otherwise claim a privileged service identity) and one pins a data-duplication property on the ingest→catalog commit door. A regression in any of them ships green.
cross_service.recommendation: Add `"services/catalog/tests", "services/lineage/tests"` to `[tool.pytest.ini_options] testpaths` and run them once to confirm they still pass (test_commit_idempotency drives a real local Lance dataset, so check it is not slow-marked-worthy). Then add an invariant test — the estate already has `tests/unit/test_e2e_collection_gate.py` as the pattern — asserting that every `services/*/tests` and `packages/*/tests` directory on disk appears in `testpaths`, so the next service cannot repeat this.

cross_service.title: `known-first-party` names 8 of the 19 real first-party import names — 11 packages sort into the third-party block
cross_service.why: Ruff's `I` rule is in `select`, so every module importing one of the eleven is sorted with those imports in the third-party block. The in-file comment at pyproject.toml:143-152 documents this as a deliberate deferral (adding them turns 1 I001 into 206 across 172 files), so this is a tracked debt rather than an oversight — but it is still a live inconsistency: eight names get first-party treatment and eleven do not, which makes the import block of a catalog module and a compute module structurally different for no reason a reader can see.
cross_service.recommendation: Land the deferred pass as its own commit exactly as the comment prescribes: add all eleven names, then `uvx ruff check --select I --fix`, nothing else in the diff. Do it on a quiet branch (the pre-commit hook passes no filenames, so it reddens every in-flight branch until merged).

cross_service.title: `configure_app_logging`'s allow-list is stale: `maintenance` calls it but is not on the list, while dead names `compaction` and `common` are
cross_service.why: The whole purpose of this function, per its docstring, is that the OTel SDK's root LoggingHandler never fires for INFO because nothing raises the app level from WARNING. So the maintenance service's entire INFO tier is dropped: `maintenance_sweep` (routes.py:68), `reconcile_clean` (routes.py:125), `optimize_indices_disabled_by_policy`, `cleanup_disabled_by_policy`, the lance-trace bridge lines. Those are exactly the records an operator needs to answer 'did the sweep run and what did it compact' — the service is the estate's only destructive background job and it is observably silent.
cross_service.recommendation: Replace the hand-maintained tuple with the real set: add `maintenance`, `ingest`, `flows`, `compute`, `controlplane`, `gateway`; drop `compaction` and `common`. Better: derive it — the caller already knows its own package, so make the signature `configure_app_logging(*packages: str)` defaulting to the caller's top-level package via `__name__.split('.')[0]`, which cannot drift when a service is renamed. Add a unit test asserting each entrypoint module's root package logger is at INFO after import.

cross_service.title: The fleet's own logging setup targets logger names that no longer exist, and `setup_otel` exports no logs at all despite claiming to
cross_service.why: Two independent halves of the same gap: the fleet raises the level of two loggers that do not exist (so the handler-level config is a no-op), and even at the right level there is no OTLP log pipeline in the fleet path. The result is that gateway/compute/controlplane/flows/ingest ship zero logs to GreptimeDB while the lance plane ships them — an asymmetry that is invisible until an incident, and the docstring actively asserts the opposite.
cross_service.recommendation: Either (a) make the fleet match the lance plane — switch `chart/templates/fleet.yaml` to `command: ["opentelemetry-instrument", "uvicorn"]` and have `make_service_app` call `configure_app_logging` (fixed per X4) instead of `_setup_logging`, then delete `_setup_logging`; or (b) wire a `LoggerProvider` + `BatchLogRecordProcessor(OTLPLogExporter())` + root `LoggingHandler` inside `setup_otel` and fix its logger names. Pick one path for the whole estate; correct the `otel.py` docstring to match whichever ships.

cross_service.title: `search` is the only explorer service with no authn/authz code path at all — the chart's estate-wide OIDC/FGA env has nothing to bind to
cross_service.why: The chart comment's premise — 'a service with no such route is unaffected' — is exactly the hole for search: on an `auth.enabled` estate, viewer gates corpus metadata and bytes on `can_get_metadata`/`can_read_data` and annotator gates its task plane, while search returns actual search HITS (row content, transcript text, filter facets) from the same corpora to any caller that can reach the gateway. `viewer/api/security.py:1` documents this precise posture as the defect it was written to close ('A corpus LIST is itself sensitive: it names data someone may not know exists') — search still has the pre-fix state, and unlike a misconfiguration it cannot be closed by any values change.
cross_service.recommendation: Give search the same door its two siblings already have and share: change `SearchSettings` to inherit `GovernedAuthSettings`, add `search/api/security.py` built on `service_kit.governed.deps.make_auth_deps` (the module viewer already uses — no new mechanism), and gate the search router on `can_read_data` for the resolved target table via a router-level `dependencies=[...]` so no endpoint can be added ungated. Add a unit test asserting all three explorer apps refuse an unauthenticated request when `RASK_OIDC_ENABLED=true`.

cross_service.title: gateway and ingest have no Settings class — 46 of the estate's 67 raw env reads live in those two services, several captured at import time
cross_service.why: House rule 9 puts config in one pydantic-settings class per service; here the two busiest services have none, so there is no single place to see what a gateway or ingest pod is configured with, no validation (a malformed `RASK_INGEST_MAX_ACK_PENDING` raises `ValueError` at import, crash-looping the pod with a bare traceback), and no test seam — the module-scope reads mean a test must manipulate `os.environ` before import order it does not control. The three independent reads of the delimiter are how two modules end up disagreeing about a table name.
cross_service.recommendation: Add `gateway/config.py` with a `GatewaySettings(BaseSettings)` (api_prefix, the 9 upstream URLs, dapr_enabled, dapr_http_port, sidecar_only_routes) built once in the lifespan onto `app.state.settings`, and have `_routes`/`_target_base` take it as a parameter — this also removes the per-request env read. Add `ingest/config.py` with an `IngestSettings(BaseSettings)` covering the RASK_INGEST_*/RASK_CATALOG_*/RASK_NATS_* knobs, built in `create_app` and read through a dep; keep `IngestAuthSettings` as-is. Fold the three delimiter reads into one setting.

cross_service.title: The four `make_service_app` services expose liveness only, and the chart points BOTH k8s probes at it — no readiness, no drain signal, though `service_kit.probes` exists for exactly this
cross_service.why: Readiness that is identical to liveness means the pod is put in rotation the instant the socket answers — before flows has decided whether the Dapr workflow lane is up, before compute has its Ray client, before ingest has resolved its FGA store (`_resolve_fga_client` runs in the lifespan and its failure mode is documented as '503 every request') — and it stays in rotation for the whole graceful-drain window, so a rollout drops in-flight requests the lance plane's rollouts do not. The estate already paid for this lesson once: `ingest/health.py:3` records a pod stuck at 1/2 forever because the probe path and the app disagreed.
