cross_service.recommendation: Have `make_service_app` set `app.state.startup_complete=False`/`shutting_down=False` in its lifespan wrapper (it already wraps every injected lifespan at `service_kit/__init__.py:107-120`, so this is four lines in one place) and mount `service_kit.probes.router` unconditionally. Then split the chart: `readinessProbe → /readyz`, `livenessProbe → /livez`, keeping `/api/health` as the frontend-facing badge. Gateway's `/healthz` can stay bespoke but should gain the same two paths for the same reason.

cross_service.title: `make_service_app` publishes /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json unconditionally, while all seven lance services gate them behind a *_DOCS setting
cross_service.why: Ingest's OpenAPI describes a data-writing control API whose door was itself a documented prod-blocker, and flows' describes the run-execution surface; the gateway proxies `/api/*` to all four, so both are reachable from the public edge in every deployment. Beyond exposure, the asymmetry means an operator who sets `*_DOCS=false` across the estate reasonably believes the schema surface is closed and it is not.
cross_service.recommendation: Add `docs_enabled: bool = Field(default=True, alias="RASK_DOCS")` to `service_kit.config.Settings` and gate all three URLs in `make_service_app` on it, matching the lance apps. Set it false in the chart's prod overlay for the fleet, the same way the lance `*_DOCS` values are handled.

cross_service.title: Seven env-var prefixes across twelve services, with `LANCE_*` leaking into three services that otherwise use their own
cross_service.why: House rule 9 says `RASK_*` with no legacy prefixes; the `LANCE_*` family is inherited from the lance-ns merge and is now the estate's largest config surface. The practical cost is not aesthetic: an operator setting `MEDALLION_AUDIT_ENABLED` gets silence (pydantic `extra="ignore"`), and the same knob (`fga_api_url`, `oidc_issuer`, secret-store name) exists under four different names in four services, so a values change has to be applied four ways and any one of them can be missed — which is precisely how the `RASK_OIDC_DISCOVERY_URL` gap in `ingest/__init__.py:100-116` survived across five services that had it and one that did not.
cross_service.recommendation: Do not rename in flight. Instead: (1) record the prefix-per-service table in `.claude/skills/rask-architecture` so it is a known map rather than a discovery; (2) fix the two genuine leaks now — give lineage and medallion `LINEAGE_AUDIT_ENABLED`/`MEDALLION_AUDIT_ENABLED` with the `LANCE_AUDIT_ENABLED` value as a deprecated alias (pydantic `AliasChoices`); (3) when the LANCE→RASK rename is scheduled, do it with `AliasChoices(new, old)` per field so no deployment breaks mid-rollout.

cross_service.title: ingest installs both handler sets, so its 422 body silently differs from its three fleet siblings
viewer/search test-seam factories build a different app than production — no problem handlers, no probes — so the exact regression their prod comments describe is untestable
cross_service.why: Any test using these factories exercises an app whose error taxonomy, probe surface and (for search) CORS differ from what ships. The 500-instead-of-401 bug was found live, not by the suite, and with these factories in place an identical future omission would again be invisible. This is the same class as `ingest/health.py:3`'s 'nothing about the image, the render, or the unit suite was wrong'.
cross_service.recommendation: Collapse the seam: extract one `build_app(settings, state) -> FastAPI` used by BOTH the module-level `app` and the test factories, so there is a single wiring list. If a test genuinely needs a stripped app, have it opt out explicitly (`build_app(..., with_probes=False)`) rather than by construction. Do the same for `create_viewer_state`/`create_search_app`.

cross_service.title: The three media apps' lifespans have no try/finally around `yield`, unlike the five other lance apps
The governed-auth bootstrap (OIDC verifier + FGA provision/make_client) is copy-pasted into 8 lifespans
cross_service.why: The estate has already paid for this twice, and both incidents are written into the comments. medallion/producer.py:74 records that 'the medallion alone re-provisioned on every boot, minting a model version per pod restart'; ingest/__init__.py:100-116 records that ingest was the single door missing split-horizon discovery, so every signed-in ingest died with a ConnectError surfaced as `{"message":"Internal Error"}`. Eight copies of an authorization-bootstrap mean a fix lands in one and the other seven keep the bug; the eight already differ in whether construction failures are fatal (catalog/lineage raise, viewer/annotator swallow into a logged 503, maintenance returns None, ingest defers to a resolve-by-name path).
cross_service.recommendation: Add `service_kit.governed.bootstrap.wire_governed_auth(app, settings, *, provision: bool = True) -> None` to service-kit (it already owns `fga`, `oidc` and `GovernedAuthSettings`, and takes no new dependency). It should own the pinned-else-provision decision, the split-horizon override, the timeout, and the failure posture as an explicit parameter — `provision=False` for the read-only consumers (ingest, maintenance) that must never author a model, matching the `fga.resolve` vs `fga.provision` split that already exists at packages/service-kit/src/service_kit/governed/fga.py:278. Then delete the eight blocks. service-kit base stays lance/ray-free: `fga`/`oidc` are already under `governed/`.

cross_service.title: lineage re-implements service_kit's service-door authenticator, and the two copies have already diverged
cross_service.why: This is the estate's service-to-service authentication primitive — the one that decides whether a caller may claim `service-trainer` (writer on `namespace:models`). Its own docstrings record that the lessons it encodes 'were each paid for once and must not be re-learned per service'. With two copies, they are being re-learned: the entry-guard divergence means a caller supplying `x-lance-service-identity: anything` gets a hard 403 from lineage where the catalog falls through to OIDC, and any future hardening (a new privileged-subject rule, a new laundering path) must be found in two files rather than one. A security control with a second copy is a security control with a stale copy.
cross_service.recommendation: Delete `lineage/api/security.py::_service_principal` and `ServicePrincipal`; call `service_kit.governed.dapr_auth.service_principal(...)` as catalog/api/security.py:96 already does, passing `dedicated_token=_dedicated_token`. The only real difference is the exception taxonomy (lineage raises `lance_namespace` typed errors, the shared helper raises `HTTPException`) — resolve it by having the shared helper raise the `lance_namespace` types, since every consumer of this door installs `service_kit.lakehouse.ns_errors.install_problem_handlers` anyway.

cross_service.title: `authorize_produce` and `authorize_ingest` are two ~120-line copies of one dual-auth door
cross_service.why: The docstring's own reasoning — 'two different answers to one question is how an estate ends up with a weak door and a strong one' — is the argument for sharing, not for copying. Both doors gate write paths into a project's tiers, both encode the measured gateway-laundering bypass (produce_auth.py:86-91 cites the ingest measurement: '403 straight to the pod, 202 through the gateway'), and both must be fixed together forever. The order of checks already differs: produce_auth refuses the public caller BEFORE the token compare (line 93), ingest/auth compares the token first and refuses after (lines 126/135), so a request carrying both a valid service token and an Authorization header takes different paths through the two doors.
cross_service.recommendation: Extract `service_kit.governed.project_door.authorize_project_write(...)` taking `(request, *, expected_token, dapr_api_token, authorization, dapr_caller_app_id, project, service_project, oidc_enabled, fga_client, action="ingest"|"produce")` and returning None or raising the typed errors. Both call sites shrink to a settings-binding wrapper, exactly as `service_kit.governed.deps.make_auth_deps` already does for the read-side checker. Keep the `action` string only for the audit label and the denial message.

cross_service.title: catalog's `_bucket_client` builds boto3 directly, bypassing packages/storage and losing s3v4, path-style and timeouts
cross_service.why: Two independent problems. (1) HOUSE-RULE-8: `packages/storage.s3_client` is the canonical wrapper and service code must not import boto3 — maintenance already complies for the same operation, so this is drift, not a considered exception. (2) The omitted `addressing_style: "path"` is the exact configuration `service_kit/lakehouse/objectfs.py:32` warns about — 'RustFS/MinIO reject virtual-hosted signing with 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch' — and boto3's default `auto` prefers virtual-hosted addressing for DNS-compatible bucket names, which is precisely what a warehouse bucket is. The missing connect/read timeouts also violate HOUSE-RULE-10 on a blocking call that runs in a threadpool during warehouse create/delete.
cross_service.recommendation: Replace `_bucket_client` with `storage.s3_client(storage_options["endpoint"], access_key=..., secret_key=...)`. If the vending paths genuinely need an STS client rather than an S3 one (vending.py:195/251 do), leave them but move the STS-client construction behind a named helper in `packages/storage` too, so `import boto3` appears in exactly one package.

cross_service.title: `control_emit.py` exists twice, near-verbatim (136 and 141 lines), and only one copy is tested
cross_service.why: The stated constraint is right and the conclusion is wrong: the answer to 'maintenance may not import the catalog' is to put the emitter where the event model already lives — `service_kit.control_events` — not to copy it. The cost is already visible in test coverage: `tests/unit/test_control_events.py` imports only `catalog.core.control_emit`, so the maintenance copy's timeout bound, its failure counter and its error-swallow are never exercised; the maintenance module is only reached as `NoopControlEmitter` in `tests/unit/test_reconcile_route.py`.
cross_service.recommendation: Move the whole module to `service_kit/control_emit.py` beside `control_events.py` and `dapr_publish.py` (both already service-kit-owned, both already imported by each copy), parameterising the meter/counter name on a `service: str` argument. Delete both service copies. No dependency weight is added — `dapr.aio.clients` and `opentelemetry.metrics` are already service-kit imports via `dapr_publish` and `lakehouse/outbox_metrics.py`.

cross_service.title: Four byte-identical `health.py` liveness routers
cross_service.why: flows/health.py:8 and ingest/health.py:4 both explain the reason for the copy — '`make_service_app` supplies no health route; every service mounts its own' — and ingest/health.py:1-12 records what the missing copy cost: the first in-cluster deploy sat at 1/2 forever because the chart probes `/api/health` and the app had no such route, so 'a Deployment that looks deployed and serves nothing'. Four copies of a route whose absence is that expensive is exactly the shape that produces a fifth service with no health route.
cross_service.recommendation: Add the router to `service_kit.probes` (which already owns `/livez` + `/readyz` and imports the same `Liveness` model) as `health_router`, and have `make_service_app` mount it by default with an opt-out. That closes the class of bug ingest hit rather than documenting it four times.

cross_service.title: The Arrow-IPC-stream encoder is hand-written at 7 sites, and the media-type string at 6
cross_service.why: Two of the copies carry the same warning in their docstrings — writer.py:152 and lakehouse.py:56 both say an IPC *file* body 'fails their reader' and only a *stream* works — which means the encoding is a contract with the catalog's write endpoints, and a contract asserted in seven places is a contract nobody owns. The media-type constant is worse: `catalog/api/load_shed.py:34` holds it as `bytes` for header matching while the others hold `str`, so a change to the wire type would have to be found in six spellings across two types.
cross_service.recommendation: Put `arrow_stream_bytes(table: pa.Table) -> bytes` and `ARROW_STREAM_MEDIA_TYPE` / `ARROW_FILE_MEDIA_TYPE` in a new `service_kit/arrow.py` (pyarrow is already a hard service-kit dependency via `lakehouse/objectfs.py` and `lancekit/`). Replace all seven encoders and all six literals. Keep the file-vs-stream asymmetry documented in that one module.

cross_service.title: The OIDC/FGA settings block is re-declared in 4 services despite `GovernedAuthSettings` existing for it
cross_service.why: The types have already split: `fga_store_id` is `str | None = None` in catalog/lineage/maintenance and `str = ""` in medallion (config.py:113), so the pinned-else-provision test `if not (store_id and model_id)` happens to work for both only by accident. Three services (annotator, viewer, ingest) DID adopt the mixin, so the estate now runs two vocabularies for one concept, and `tests/unit/test_oidc_discovery_parity.py` exists solely to police the gap. A settings field added to the mixin silently does not reach four services.
cross_service.recommendation: Mix `GovernedAuthSettings` into all four remaining settings classes. The env-prefix divergence is the real work: keep the `LANCE_*` aliases as the estate vocabulary (that is what the mixin already declares and what the chart already sets) and add per-service aliases only where a value must genuinely differ per pod, using pydantic's `AliasChoices` so both spellings resolve during the transition.

cross_service.title: `apply_dapr_secrets` is written four times, once inline in a lifespan
cross_service.why: HOUSE-RULE-7 makes the secret store the sole, fail-closed source, so this is security-relevant plumbing. The copies have already diverged on the fail-closed edge: catalog raises at boot when the store is off and the env key is empty, maintenance raises at service.py:124 (a third location), and medallion only warns via a model validator at config.py:249 that is skipped entirely when `secrets_from_dapr` is set. One of the four therefore has a path to booting with an empty S3 key.
cross_service.recommendation: Add `service_kit.governed.secrets.apply_s3_secret(settings, *, require_when_disabled: bool = True) -> None` operating on a small Protocol (`secrets_from_dapr`, `dapr_secret_store`, `dapr_secret_key`, `dapr_secret_s3_field`, `s3_secret_access_key`) — the module already owns `fetch_required_secrets` and the fail-closed rule its docstring claims to be 'the one place the fail-closed rule lives'. Fold the four field blocks into a `DaprSecretSettings` mixin next to `GovernedAuthSettings`.

cross_service.title: Two OpenLineage kernels and four RunEvent builders, one of which documents itself as a duplicate
cross_service.why: service_kit/openlineage.py:12-16 records that three of these URLs had already drifted once ('SchemaDatasetFacet 1-1-1→1-2-0, DatasourceDatasetFacet and ErrorMessageRunFacet 1-0-0→1-0-1') and that a conformance test now pins them — but the test pins the SERVICE-KIT copy, not lineage-kit's. So a bump to `openlineage-python` reddens CI for one home and silently leaves the other on a stale spec version, which is exactly the failure the test was written to prevent. The duplicated `ColumnEdge` name with different arities is an active trap for anyone moving code between the two modules.
cross_service.recommendation: Make `packages/lineage-kit` the single OpenLineage kernel (it already wraps the official `openlineage.client` facet classes, so it is the more faithful home) and have `service_kit.openlineage` re-export from it, or vice versa — but pick one. Delete `service_kit/lancekit/openlineage.py::build_run_event` now that the merge it was hedging against has landed. Rename one of the two `ColumnEdge` aliases immediately regardless of the larger consolidation; that one is cheap and prevents a real mistake. Dependency note: lineage-kit pulls `openlineage-python`, which service_kit/openlineage.py:9-11 says is deliberately dev-only and kept out of service images — so if service-kit becomes the importer, the dependency must be an extra, not a base requirement.

cross_service.title: The catalog identifier delimiter `$` is declared nine times through three different mechanisms
cross_service.why: The comments already state the stakes. maintenance/core/config.py:76 and medallion/core/config.py:186 both warn that 'a mismatch addresses a DIFFERENT table rather than failing' — a silent wrong-object read, not an error. `service_kit/governed/fga.py:137` makes it sharper still: 'The seed (grant) path and the check path MUST agree byte-for-byte on the id they use, otherwise a grant lands on `table:a$b` while the check looks up `table:a/b` and silently denies.' Nine declarations across five env-var names cannot be kept in agreement by convention, and two of them are literals that no env var can correct.
cross_service.recommendation: Declare `CATALOG_DELIMITER` once in service-kit beside `service_kit.governed.fga.canonical_object_id` (which is already the estate's id-canonicaliser and already takes `delimiter` as a keyword). Have every settings class default its `delimiter` field to that constant under a single alias, and delete the two hardcoded literals plus the three ingest `os.getenv` calls — HOUSE-RULE-9 forbids scattered env reads outside the settings module regardless of the duplication.

cross_service.title: The lance-service entrypoint is hand-assembled eight times; there is no `make_lance_service_app`
cross_service.why: HOUSE-RULE-6 sanctions the two layouts, not the absence of a factory for the second one. `make_service_app` (packages/service-kit/src/service_kit/__init__.py:90) already proves the shape works — it owns logging, handlers, middleware, OTel, the Dapr client and the probe wiring — and the four services that use it get all of that for free. The eight that do not have each drifted: viewer/annotator/search never call `configure_audit`, only catalog/lineage/medallion/maintenance call `assert_app_token_configured`, and medallion/mover.py:79 reads `_settings.docs_enabled` where its sibling producer.py:107 reads a separate `_docs` local. The comment 'like the catalog' appearing five times is the tell.
cross_service.recommendation: Add `make_lance_service_app(*, title, routers, lifespan, ready_check=None, docs_enabled)` to service-kit, composing `configure_app_logging` + the docs gate + `install_problem_handlers` + `make_probes_router` + the startup/shutdown flag discipline. It is a sibling of `make_service_app`, not a replacement — the difference is only the error taxonomy (`ns_errors` vs `exceptions`) and the docs gate. That leaves each `main.py` holding only its genuinely service-specific lifespan body.

cross_service.title: annotator re-implements `service_kit.governed.deps.make_auth_deps`, the module extracted from it
cross_service.why: The shared module carries a hard-won correctness note the annotator copy does not: deps.py:19-32 forbids `from __future__ import annotations` in that file because deferred annotations silently demote the injected settings dependency to a QUERY PARAM, so every gated route answers 422 instead of authorizing — a bug that shipped and was invisible to tests that override the dependency. annotator/api/security.py:18 DOES carry `from __future__ import annotations`; it survives only because it binds `SettingsDep` at module scope rather than through a factory parameter. That is one refactor away from reproducing the exact bug the shared module was hardened against.
cross_service.recommendation: Replace annotator/api/security.py's `authenticate`/`current_subject`/`get_checker`/`FgaChecker`/`ANONYMOUS_SUBJECT`/`raw_bearer` with `make_auth_deps(SettingsDep)` as viewer already does, keeping only `get_fga_client`/`FgaClientDep` (the write-side seam the shared module deliberately does not expose) — and consider moving that seam into `AuthDeps` too, since it is the same three-outcome decision.

cross_service.title: The same hand-rolled HTTP backoff loop exists in packages/storage and services/ingest, while tenacity is the estate's retry layer
cross_service.why: HOUSE-RULE-10 centralises retries on tenacity, and service-kit already does. These two copies are neither centralised nor equivalent: they disagree on which 4xx are retryable, and neither uses jitter, so N concurrent page fetches against a rate-limited IIIF endpoint retry in lockstep — the thundering-herd case `wait_exponential_jitter` exists to prevent. The `assert last is not None` in both would also be compiled out under `python -O`, turning an exhausted-retry path into an implicit `raise None` TypeError.
cross_service.recommendation: Extract one `service_kit.http_retry.fetch_with_retry(client, url, *, attempts, base_delay, retryable_4xx)` built on tenacity's `Retrying` + `retry_if_exception` + `wait_exponential_jitter` (the exact shape governed/secrets.py:59 already uses), and call it from both. Settle the retryable-4xx set once — 408/425/429 is the correct superset, so ingest's is right and storage's is missing two.

cross_service.title: The Dapr-workflow scheduler is written twice, and the two copies' timeouts have already drifted
cross_service.why: HOUSE-RULE-7 makes Dapr Workflow the estate's durable-orchestration primitive, so this scheduling adapter is platform plumbing, not service logic — and the divergent timeout is the proof that copies drift silently. ingest/api.py:173 surfaces its value in a user-facing message ('the workflow engine did not accept run {run_id} within {SCHEDULE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s'), so the two services now promise different things for the same operation with no reason recorded for the difference.
cross_service.recommendation: Add `service_kit.workflow.schedule_workflow(workflow, *, instance_id, payload, timeout_seconds)` holding the lazy import, the `to_thread` hop and the `wait_for` bound, with one default. `dapr-ext-workflow` is already a dependency of both consumers; keep the import lazy inside the function so service-kit's base stays free of it.

cross_service.title: viewer, search and annotator share a copy-pasted media-service lifespan
cross_service.why: The three files call themselves a template, which is the honest description of a factory that was never written. The copies have already diverged in a way that matters: `httpx.Client()` is constructed with NO default timeout at all three sites (plus a fourth at viewer/main.py:112), relying on every call site to remember a per-call `timeout=` — annotator/api/v1/endpoints/assist.py:376 and jobs.py:115/132 and viewer/api/v1/endpoints/system.py:59 all do, but nothing enforces it, and HOUSE-RULE-10 asks for the bound on the client. Only annotator installs the Dapr actor extension; only viewer defines the `create_*_app` test seams.
cross_service.recommendation: Add `service_kit.media.app.make_media_app(*, title, router, extra_lifespan=None)` beside the existing `service_kit/media/{config,deps,middleware,state}.py` — the media layer already owns everything else these three files share. Give the shared `AppState` an `httpx.Client(timeout=...)` default sourced from the media settings so the bound cannot be forgotten by a fourth service.

cross_service.title: One Dapr secret store is named by seven different env vars sharing one default
cross_service.why: maintenance/core/control_emit.py:19-21 names the failure mode this creates: 'the pubsub component's `scopes` must list this service's Dapr app-id, or the sidecar rejects every publish (same class as the secret-store scoping rule)'. Renaming or re-scoping the store means finding seven env vars across five services and two mechanisms, and a miss fails at the sidecar — which, for the best-effort paths, fails silently. The three module-scope `os.getenv` reads also break HOUSE-RULE-9 outright and are evaluated at import time, so a test cannot override them.
cross_service.recommendation: Fold `dapr_secret_store` / `dapr_secret_key` into the `DaprSecretSettings` mixin proposed in DUP-09 under one alias (`RASK_DAPR_SECRET_STORE`, with `AliasChoices` covering the legacy names during migration), and route lineage/api/security.py:85, viewer/objects.py:84 and ingest/catalog_service.py:75 through it instead of reading env directly.
